justification: The Housing SEPP eligibility route reported every form eligible once its zone matched and no lot row stopped it. A form with no lot standard in the dataset therefore passed by default: until 2026-09-15 that was manor_house, whose rows were really section 108 standards for independent living units, so users were told a Manor House was eligible, with a 'SEPP allows 9.5m vs LEP' override. The rows were relabelled in production on 2026-09-15; without this change the route would now say the same about independent living units. Cross-review then showed both engines exempted dual occupancy and secondary dwellings from the guard, so a missing lot row for them also passed as eligible.

falsifiable_check.command: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/api/housing-sepp-unassessable-forms.test.ts && cd .. && python -m pytest tests/test_housing_sepp_eligibility.py -o addopts= -k missing
falsifiable_check.fails_when: A form with no lot standard in the dataset (other than dwelling houses in the Python engine, and the station-distance apartment forms) comes back eligible, or a SEPP-over-LEP override is listed for a form that was not found eligible.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Against the route on main, 2 of the new tests failed: independent_living_unit came back eligible in R2, and the overrides for a lot outside a reform area listed independent_living_unit and residential_flat_r1r2. With the dual-occupancy exemption restored, 'exempts no form' fails in jest and test_dual_occupancy_missing_its_lot_row_is_not_passed fails in pytest. With the fix: 15 jest tests across the two eligibility suites and 101 pytest tests across the five eligibility, upzoning and brief suites pass.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: Housing SEPP (in force 15 Sep 2026) section 108 is headed 'Non-discretionary development standards for independent living units' and states the 9.5m height, 0.5:1 FSR, landscaped area and 15% deep soil standards that the table had filed as manor house rules. housing_sepp_standards holds a min_lot_size row for dual_occupancy and secondary_dwelling, and none for independent_living_unit.

pre_impl.existing_data: housing_sepp_standards: 45 rows across 8 forms after the 2026-09-15 correction. min_lot_size present for dual_occupancy, multi_dwelling, residential_flat_r1r2, secondary_dwelling and terraces; absent for independent_living_unit and the two station-distance residential_flat_r3r4 forms. No dwelling_house rows.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The route assumed every form in the table carries a lot standard, so reaching the end of the checks meant eligible. The Python engine guarded that case but exempted dual occupancy and secondary dwellings, which do carry a lot standard, so a dropped row there passed silently too.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Same guard in both engines: a form with no min_lot_size is not assessed, except the station-distance apartment forms (their own check) and, in Python, dwelling houses (no SEPP lot minimum; no such rows exist, so the route needs no exemption). Overrides only for eligible forms, as the brief does. No new query and no change to the response shape; one display name and one page label added.

functions.name: POST
functions.input: zoneCode, lotSize, lotWidth, optional stationDistance, isLMRArea, lepHeight and lepFsr.
functions.output: One eligibility result per form applicable to the zone; a form with no lot standard in the dataset (other than the station-distance apartment forms) is isEligible false with assessmentStatus 'not_assessed'; overrides only for forms found eligible.
functions.if_none: No standards rows returns no forms and no overrides; a failed read returns the existing 500 error.

functions.name: evaluate_eligibility
functions.input: zone code, lot area and width, coordinates, heritage flag and optional gate inputs.
functions.output: Per-form FormEligibility; a form outside {dwelling_houses, dwelling_house} and the station-distance apartment forms with no min_lot_size is ineligible and unconfirmed with the 'not in the dataset' reason.
functions.if_none: Unchanged: non-residential zone or an unreadable standards table returns [].

values.if_missing: For any form that is not a station-distance apartment form, the result is not assessed instead of eligible.
A form not found eligible gets no SEPP-over-LEP override line.

queries.purpose: Read every Housing SEPP standard with its form, zones, reform-area flag and clause to decide each form's eligibility.
queries.where_clause: FROM housing_sepp_standards ORDER BY development_type, standard_type (unchanged; all 45 standards are read and filtered by zones in code)

break_it.scenario: A form in the table has no lot standard in the dataset (independent living units since the 2026-09-15 relabel; manor houses before it).
break_it.what_happens: Every check is skipped and the form is reported eligible, with its Housing SEPP standard read as an entitlement for that form in any listed zone.
break_it.how: The route returns not assessed for such a form, as housing_sepp_eligibility.py does. test 'is not reported eligible, and says it was not assessed'; removing the guard failed 3 tests.

break_it.scenario: A form that does carry a lot standard loses its min_lot_size row after an incomplete import, e.g. dual occupancy (cross-review HIGH on the first push).
break_it.what_happens: With dual occupancy exempt from the guard, the form is reported eligible on any lot without the lot threshold ever being checked.
break_it.how: No form is exempt in the route; in the Python engine only dwelling houses are, since the SEPP sets them no lot minimum. Re-exempting dual occupancy failed 'exempts no form' (jest) and test_dual_occupancy_missing_its_lot_row_is_not_passed (pytest).
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/api/housing-sepp-unassessable-forms.test.ts -t 'exempts no form' && cd .. && python -m pytest tests/test_housing_sepp_eligibility.py -o addopts= -k dual_occupancy_missing

break_it.scenario: The guard catches the station-distance apartment forms, which have no lot standard row but their own distance check.
break_it.what_happens: Mid-rise apartments near a station would never be reported eligible.
break_it.how: The residential_flat_r3r4 exemption is kept; removing it failed 'leaves the station-distance apartment forms to their own check'.

break_it.scenario: A SEPP-over-LEP height or FSR override is listed for a form the property cannot use or that was not assessed, in zones where the Housing SEPP standard exists.
break_it.what_happens: The response says the SEPP allows 9.5m over the LEP for that form, which reads as an entitlement the property does not have.
break_it.how: Overrides are built only for forms found eligible; removing the filter failed 'are listed only for forms found eligible'.

break_it.scenario: The unassessable form is reported as a confirmed negative instead of a check that did not run.
break_it.what_happens: A consumer reading assessmentStatus would tell the user the form is ineligible, a finding nobody made.
break_it.how: assessmentStatus is 'not_assessed'; changing it to 'ineligible' failed 2 tests.

break_it.scenario: Narrowing the Python exemption also removes dwelling houses, which have no SEPP lot minimum.
break_it.what_happens: A dwelling house would stop being reported eligible on every lot.
break_it.how: _BASE_FORMS keeps dwelling_houses/dwelling_house; emptying the set failed 3 existing pytest tests (including test_dwelling_house_is_eligible_with_no_lot_data_and_no_gates).

mutation_analysis: Route (jest, new suite + housing-sepp-lmr-default): guard removed -> 3 failed; dual occupancy exempt again -> 1 failed; station-distance forms not exempt -> 1 failed; overrides for every form -> 1 failed; status 'ineligible' instead of 'not_assessed' -> 2 failed; unmutated 15 passed. Python (pytest, eligibility + upzoning + brief suites): dual_occupancy back in _BASE_FORMS -> 1 failed; _BASE_FORMS emptied -> 3 failed; unmutated 101 passed. The jest fixture takes its zones from HOUSING_SEPP_LMR.ELIGIBLE_ZONES, the route's own set, rather than a new literal list (zone-code lint). All files restored after each mutation.
residual_risk: The route is still a separate implementation of services/housing_sepp_eligibility.py (DQ-30 consolidation candidate); the two now apply the same guard, but a future change to one will not reach the other. The route does not read stale_since, so a standard flagged stale by the law monitor is served there without the notice the Python engine carries. /api/tod/parking-rates still selects columns housing_sepp_standards does not have and reports its SEPP tier as degraded on every call; left as is because making it answer would present the conditional 0.5-space minimum in section 179(2)(c) as an overriding rate.

post_merge.db_reset: No reset. The data half was applied to production on 2026-09-15 by a guarded one-off script (backup data/db_rollback_backups/housing_sepp_standards_pre_correction_2026-09-15_2044.csv): 13 standards re-cited to today's Housing SEPP with the quoted text recorded, 4 relabelled manor_house -> independent_living_unit, 1 relabelled max_height -> setback_height_threshold; total unchanged at 45, none stale.
post_merge.manual_verify: POST /api/housing-sepp/eligibility with {"zoneCode":"R2","lotSize":600,"lotWidth":15,"isLMRArea":true} lists Independent Living Units as not assessed and no Manor House entry; /planning-standards shows 'Independent Living Units' with 4 standards.
